clue.text: Angry, accepting running clubs train here in London?

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it on board, so the first word takes the others in front of itself

blocks.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
haring is dashing along like a hare
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: An irate jogger, member of some running clubs, in training somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb for an athlete, but it is the noun: CHARING CROSS is a main-line railway station in central London, where trains start and stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway terminus is precisely a spot where passenger services begin and end their journeys, hence the question mark for this indirect description.

clue.text: Criminal record admitted by rotter before appeal

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so one piece goes within another
coming before means placed earlier in the line, so one piece precedes the next

blocks.note: a cur is a contemptible man
an LP is a long-playing record
IT means sex appeal, as in having 'it'

explanation.surface: A villain's criminal record gets mentioned by some scoundrel just before a court appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal record' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the first word is the definition and 'record' is wordplay. IT for sex appeal is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person responsible for an offence, so the noun sense of criminal fits as a direct synonym.

clue.text: Scrap with Rear Admiral, turning round

indicators.note: turning about makes something face the other way, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: to scrap a law or contract is to cancel it
RA is the abbreviation for Rear Admiral

explanation.surface: A quarrel with a senior naval officer who has just spun about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' poses as a fight and 'round' looks like part of 'turning round'; in fact 'round' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular describes something shaped like a ring, so it is an adjective synonym for circular or round.

clue.text: Account about king, exclusive figure in Bible

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a British tax-free savings scheme
R stands for rex, Latin for king
elite means select or exclusive

explanation.surface: A story about a monarch who was a figure of exclusive status in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British savings account, known as an Individual Savings Account; the king goes inside it before the word for select.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites are the people of ancient Israel, so any one of them is a person found throughout the Old Testament.

clue.text: Foremost of gymnasts, this person’s showing flexibility

indicators.note: foremost means the very front, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
the setter speaking of themself: this person has, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: The leading gymnast in a squad displays remarkable suppleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' means the setter, I, and the 's is 'has', not a possessive, giving I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Give as a noun means the capacity to bend or yield under pressure, as in a mattress with some give.

clue.text: Soldiers trounced and sent elsewhere

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps
routed means heavily defeated

explanation.surface: An army unit is crushed in battle and posted to another front.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the standard crossword shorthand for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute traffic or mail is to direct it along a different path, so it has been dispatched somewhere other than planned.

clue.text: Caspian, say, penning letter in ink

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: the Caspian is an example of a sea
pi is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: Someone by the Caspian writing a letter with ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' suggests writing, which fits the ink, but it means enclosing; the letter is Greek rather than a missive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the brown pigment obtained from cuttlefish secretions, historically used as a drawing and writing ink.

clue.text: Japanese teacher is seen after doing some translation

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so these letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Japanese tutor is observed once some translation work has been done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is seen' looks like the verb of the sentence, but those two words are the raw letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensei is the Japanese word for a master or instructor, used in English especially for martial arts instructors.

clue.text: Be nosy, say, when eating a brownie, oddly

indicators.note: eating takes food inside, so one piece swallows the others
dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves only those in even places

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, which is what 'say' signals
taken as written
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks prying questions while munching a chocolate brownie in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' here means losing the odd letters, keeping the even ones. 'Be nosy' is the definition, so the answer is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is a British informal verb meaning to eavesdrop, listening in on conversations that are none of your business.

clue.text: Short path followed by someone moving stock car

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter goes
followed by means another piece comes next in the sequence

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow path, here lacking its last letter
a drover herds livestock to market

explanation.surface: A shortcut taken by a farmhand herding cattle, or perhaps a stock-car racer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock car' looks like a racing term, but 'stock' belongs to the wordplay (livestock) and 'car' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Land Rover is a British make of four-wheel-drive vehicle, so it is a specific example of an automobile.

clue.text: Depiction of Mary’s pastry case for tea

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: a pie is a pastry dish
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Mary bakes a pastry case to go with afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastry case' reads as one phrase, but 'case' belongs to the tea. The 's after Mary is 'has', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin holding the dead body of Christ, the most famous being Michelangelo's in St Peter's.

clue.text: Painting implement for car

blocks.note: first meaning: a cylinder covered in fabric used to apply paint
second meaning: British slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A tool used to paint a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' is British slang for a Rolls-Royce, the luxury car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorators apply emulsion with a roller, and Rolls-Royce owners call their luxury motor a Roller informally.

clue.text: Game bird that’s caught was sour when cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so these letters are reworked into another order

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunted bird tasted bitter once it had been roasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes 'cooked' look literal; it signals rearrangement of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The curassow is a large turkey-like bird of Central and South American forests, hunted for its meat.

clue.text: Get rancid, tiny amount of bread and vegetable

blocks.note: milk that turns has gone sour
bread is slang for money, and one penny, 1p, is a tiny sum

explanation.surface: Food going off: a crumb of bread and some vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' suggests a loaf, but it is slang for money; 1P is one penny, written with I for the digit one.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a root crop with white flesh, eaten boiled or mashed, a common example of a vegetable.

clue.text: In a rage, nearly have hallucinations

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter falls away

blocks.note: the common idiom for perceiving what is not there, a verb plus a plural noun

explanation.surface: Someone so furious that they are almost imagining things.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for hallucinating is three words in idiom form, see things; dropping its final letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seething is to be boiling with anger, so it is an adjective synonym for furious or raging.

clue.text: Radio programme wanting small group of stars

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

blocks.note: A long-running BBC radio soap set among farmers
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A radio show that lacks a small cluster of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ARCHERS is a BBC radio soap opera about country life. 'Stars' looks like celebrities but means the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archer is the English name for Sagittarius, a constellation and sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: At least a dozen beers, or nine softly placed in bags?

indicators.note: placing something in puts it inside, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals
p is piano, the musical marking for soft
sacks are large bags

explanation.surface: A drinker buying a dozen beers or more, or else nine quietly carried in bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural: two or more packs of six cans, so at least twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is sold in multipacks of six cans, so more than one of them gives twelve or more drinks.

clue.text: Report what loaded firearm has

blocks.note: first meaning: a short official news statement
second meaning, split in two: a round of ammunition sitting inside the gun

explanation.surface: A gunshot report: the sound a loaded weapon makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' tempts toward a gunshot's bang, matching the firearm, but it means a news item; the gun half reads as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A news bulletin is a brief broadcast or published report of current events or official announcements.

clue.text: Bread sandwiches dry, I rudely interject

indicators.note: a sandwich holds filling between its slices, so one piece encloses others

blocks.note: a bun is a bread roll
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eating a sandwich of dry bread who keeps rudely interrupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' means not drinking, which is TT, short for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is an idiom for cutting into a conversation uninvited, an impolite interruption.

clue.text: Left great party in Belfast in incapacitated state

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
A1 means first-rate, with I standing for the digit
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone left a fantastic Belfast party and is now out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party, and Belfast is its capital; 'party' is political, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Being laid up is an idiom for being confined to bed by illness or injury, unable to work.

clue.text: Colour used with green design again

blocks.note: red is a colour
green and raw both mean inexperienced

explanation.surface: An artist pairs a colour with green while reworking a design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a second colour beside the first, but it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a plan or map is to sketch it a second time, so it is a verb synonym for redesign.

clue.text: Contents of gRAVy tIn — sOLId food

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so each word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: the inner three letters
the inner letter
the inner three letters

explanation.surface: What is inside a tin of gravy: solid food.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals mark the middles: strip the first and last letter of each of the three words and string what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small pasta parcels with a filling, often sold canned in tomato sauce, so they are an Italian dish.

clue.text: Funny Liberal turns up in toupee, one maybe barking?

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading from bottom to top
placed in means set inside another piece

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
funny can mean strange
a toupee is a small hairpiece

explanation.surface: A comic Liberal politician appears wearing a hairpiece, and seems quite mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like British slang for crazy, fitting the comic politician, but it is literal: a dog barks.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild dog, such as the dingo or African hunting dog, is an untamed canine that may well bark.

clue.text: In the US, exhaust detective with exercise on track

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means coming after, so the pieces follow along

blocks.note: to tail someone is to follow them
a PI is a private investigator
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: An American investigator, worn out after a workout on the running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' poses as a verb meaning tire out; it is the noun for the pipe on a car. 'Track' is the verb to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailpipe is the American word for the pipe at the back of a car through which fumes escape.

clue.text: Long to get Oscar for dramatic entertainment

blocks.note: to pant for something is to long for it
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor yearning to win an Academy Award for a dramatic role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but it is the radio code word for O. Panto is a British family stage show at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is a traditional British Christmas theatre show with slapstick, songs and audience participation, a form of stage entertainment.

clue.text: French pianist concluding finale from Rolling Stones

indicators.note: the finale is the closing part, so only the last letter is kept
concluding means coming at the end, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: the closing letter of the word
Maurice Ravel, the French composer and pianist

explanation.surface: A French pianist plays the closing number at a Rolling Stones concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stones' reads as the band, but it splits: one word supplies a letter and 'Stones' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel is a loose mass of small rounded pebbles, used for paths and driveways, so it is a collection of little rocks.

clue.text: Threats to wolves circling pack

indicators.note: circling means surrounding, so the words around it hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Dangers facing wolves that surround a pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' suggests a wolf pack, matching the surface, but it is the verb meaning to put away.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to put it away neatly in a space, so it is a verb synonym for pack.

clue.text: Run out after batting? I might do this with the Ashes

definitions.text: I might do this with the Ashes

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the preceding letters are jumbled
after means placed later, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: a batter in cricket is said to be in
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer is run out after batting, perhaps in an Ashes Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series, fitting the batting and run out; here it is literal ashes. The capital is the cricket disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place cremated remains in a funerary vessel, which is what someone does with a loved one's ashes.

clue.text: What fishermen do about onset of legal contract complaint

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the initial letter is taken
about means around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: trawlermen land cod, a common sea fish
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fishermen grumbling over the start of a legal contract dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal contract complaint' looks like a lawsuit; 'contract' is the verb meaning to come down with, and 'complaint' is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract an ailment is to fall ill with it, and the common cold is the everyday example of a minor illness.

clue.text: Celebration after move wins game — our fans out behind rugby goal?

indicators.note: moving things changes their positions, so these letters are rearranged
fanning out spreads things into a new spread, so these letters are scattered
behind means following, so the jumbled letters come after the other piece

blocks.note: rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rugby supporters celebrate a winning move by streaming out behind the posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture hides two separate shuffles of letters, then a letter drawn by its shape: the posts and crossbar form an H.
explanation.definitionFit: A house-warming is a party thrown by people who have just moved into a new home, welcoming friends to see it.
